front.title: Signed Attestation Rows of the CIRIS Epistemic Grammar and Their Relationship to SCITT

abstract.t:
The CIRIS Epistemic Grammar (CEG) records claims between parties as signed rows. Each row is one JSON object, canonicalised with the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) and signed twice: once with Ed25519 and once with ML-DSA-65, where the ML-DSA-65 signature covers the canonical bytes followed by the Ed25519 signature. Every row has one of five types: a claim, a delegation, a replacement, a withdrawal, or a recantation. A node admits a row only after a fixed set of checks, and it refuses a failing row with a named reason.
This document specifies the signed object, the signing input, the signature construction, and the admission checks, so that a second implementation can produce and verify the same bytes. It then describes how these rows relate to the roles of the SCITT architecture (RFC 9943), and where they differ from a SCITT Transparency Service. It defines no new SCITT mechanism and requests no IANA action.
